title: Cross-engine — same host, optimized MyVector
subtitle: MyVector (PR #278 NEON) · vsql_vector · pgvector · MariaDB — fashion-mnist-784, all four on one A1 host / identical 4 vCPU · 24 GB
description: The fair, apples-to-apples cross-engine view: optimized MyVector (PR #278 — NEON kernels + keepPrunedConnections), vsql_vector (VillageSQL), pgvector (Postgres 17), and MariaDB 12.3, all four benchmarked on the same A1 host (each pinned to an identical 4 vCPU / 24 GB slice, run alone), on fashion-mnist-784-euclidean (60k × 784, L2) scored against the dataset's published ground truth. This removes the cross-host confound of the other cross-engine pages (whose non-MyVector engines were measured on the A2 host) and uses MyVector's optimized build — so it answers "where does MyVector actually stand?" honestly. The matched-recall table below is the fair bottom line.
caveats: Why this page exists: the landing, glove and village cross-engine pages measured vsql/pgvector/MariaDB on the A2 host and MyVector's scalar build; mixing hosts/builds is a confound. Here every engine runs on the same A1 host / same 4 vCPU·24 GB slice with MyVector's optimized (PR #278) build — a genuinely unbiased comparison.

The honest read (matched recall@10 — the table above): MyVector is now competitive at high recall — at recall 0.999 it serves 531 QPS, beating vsql (505) and near-tying pgvector (539), and it reaches recall 1.0 at ef=100 (vs pgvector's ef=400), winning there (475 vs 272). At recall 0.98–0.995 it still trails ~2× (595 vs pgvector 1335 / vsql 1146). The original gap had two causes, and this page separates them: (1) recall efficiency — MyVector's hnswlib graph used to need ~2–4× the ef_search for a given recall; PR #278's keepPrunedConnections fix (fill each node's links back up to M instead of discarding candidates pruned by the diversity check) lifted recall-per-ef onto pgvector's curve (ef=10 0.934→0.971, ef=20 0.978→0.992), closing that half. (2) per-query overhead — MyVector's ANN query (pre-parse rewrite → UDF → JSON_TABLE → join) carries a ~1.4 ms fixed cost that caps its QPS near ~600 regardless of ef, so at low recall (few distance evals) pgvector/vsql's leaner native path wins ~2×; at high recall (more search work) that fixed cost is a small fraction and MyVector draws even or ahead. So the remaining low-recall gap is per-query execution overhead — now the single lever left; the recall-efficiency half is fixed. (The old "~2.4× everywhere" figure was scalar MyVector on a different host — both that and the recall-efficiency gap are gone here.)

vsql_vector IS included now — a true same-host 4-way: its VillageSQL dev-server (a prebuilt aarch64 tarball) was copied from A2 and run on A1 pinned to the same 4 vCPU slice with a 4 GB InnoDB buffer pool (its default pool thrashed the 188 MB index → a misleading ~2 QPS; with a right-sized pool it builds in 85 s and serves ~1200 QPS at ef=10, matching its A2 behavior). vsql's recall-per-ef tracks pgvector's (ef=10 0.974, ef=20 0.993); MyVector's keepPrunedConnections fix brings it onto that same curve (ef=10 0.971, ef=20 0.992), so MyVector now matches both on recall-per-ef.

Dataset / params: fashion-mnist-784-euclidean (ann-benchmarks), HNSW M=16, ef_construction=200 (MyVector + pgvector; MariaDB MHNSW fixes ef_construction at 10). Recall@10 vs published exact neighbors. Warm ef_search sweep; headline cards = warm ef_search=200.

MariaDB builds its HNSW online during insert (its "build" is load time, ~245 s), uses mhnsw_max_cache_size=1 GiB, and floors mhnsw_ef_search to ~2×M so its sub-floor ef=10 point is omitted (kept in the JSON under ef_search_excluded).

Index build: MyVector 67 s vs vsql 85 s vs pgvector 70 s vs MariaDB 245 s — MyVector's index build is still the fastest of the four even with the denser keepPrunedConnections graph (the kernel-only build was 46 s).
